finding.claim: reset_password_loose compares the stored reset token to the caller-supplied token with loose `==`. If $token reaches the function as a non-string, such as a JSON boolean `true` or integer `0`, the comparison can succeed without the real token. `"abc" == true` is true in every PHP version. `"abc" == 0` is true on PHP 7. Numeric-string tokens such as `"0e123" == "0e456"` also compare equal. An attacker can reset any user's password by supplying only the victim's email. The comparison is also not constant-time. Caveat: no caller or route exists in this directory, so reachability and the type of $token are unconfirmed. The function is exposed as a reset primitive.
finding.source: $email and $token arguments of reset_password_loose, presumably from an unauthenticated password-reset request, such as JSON body `{"email":"victim@x","token":true,"new":"..."}`
finding.sink: UPDATE users SET pw=... WHERE email=... (account password overwrite)

trace.note: Fetch the stored token by attacker-chosen email. The email is quoted, so there is no SQL injection.
`$row['token'] == $token` loose comparison. Type juggling makes it true for `true`, `0` on PHP 7, or `0e...` strings.
Password hash is written for the victim email. This is account takeover.

finding.guards_checked: Email is quoted via $db->quote, so SQL injection is not possible. There is no type cast on $token, which the safe variant has at line 14. No expiry, attempt limit, or caller-side validation is visible in this directory. The safe variant reset_password uses hash_equals with a (string) cast. It also has no token expiry and does not delete the token after use, so the token is reusable (lines 14-17).

verdict.guard_found: none (email quoted via $db->quote at reset.php:3/5-6 prevents SQLi only; no type cast, expiry, or caller validation on $token in the loose variant)
verdict.reason: reset.php:4 does use loose `==` on the stored token vs. $token and reset.php:5 overwrites the password, so the flaw is real if $token can be a non-string (true, or 0 on PHP 7), but reset.php is the only file, so no caller, route, or type coercion is visible to confirm reachability or the type of $token.
